hero.tagline: The Emerald City Has Always Loved the Beautiful Game
hero.description: Seattle is one of North America's premier soccer cities — home to Sounders FC, whose supporters culture sets the standard for MLS atmosphere. Lumen Field is a fortress of sound, and Seattle's Pacific Northwest culture, world-famous coffee, and stunning natural setting create a World Cup experience unlike any other host city.

stadium.name: Lumen Field
stadium.transport: Lumen Field is in downtown Seattle with excellent LINK light rail access. Take the 1 Line from anywhere in the city or directly from Sea-Tac Airport (40-minute ride) to International District/Chinatown Station — a 5-minute walk to the stadium. Also walkable from Pioneer Square and the waterfront.

quick_facts.matches_hosted: Multiple matches including group stage and advanced rounds
quick_facts.fan_hub_status: Fan hub expected at Seattle Center under the Space Needle; confirm schedules

weather.june: One of the best climates in the tournament — mild and often sunny, highs 18–22°C (64–72°F). Some overcast mornings but rarely rains in June.
weather.july: Seattle's best month. Warm, dry, and clear — highs 22–27°C (72–81°F). The city comes alive outdoors.
packing_tips: A light jacket for evenings — temperatures drop after sunset even in July
Sunscreen for outdoor events in July — Pacific Northwest sun is deceptive
Comfortable walking shoes — Seattle's hills are real
Rain layer just in case — June can have surprise showers

airports.name: Seattle-Tacoma International Airport
transfer_options: LINK 1 Line light rail: Sea-Tac Airport to International District/Chinatown in 40 minutes — the best option
Walk 5 minutes from International District/Chinatown station to Lumen Field
Rideshare from Sea-Tac to Downtown takes 25–40 minutes depending on traffic
Taxi kiosks are at the ground transportation level
airports.notes: Excellent LINK rail connection — buy an ORCA card at the airport for immediate use on rail and buses. The light rail ride is by far the most reliable transit option regardless of traffic.

match_schedule.teams_or_placeholder: Lumen Field hosts multiple matches. Full schedule after group draw.

public_transit: LINK 1 Line: International District/Chinatown station — 5-minute walk to Lumen Field
LINK runs from Sea-Tac Airport to the stadium stop in about 40 minutes
Multiple bus lines serve the SODO/Pioneer Square area on match days
rideshare: Rideshare pickup zones are on 1st Ave S south of the stadium
Post-match surge is significant — walk toward the waterfront for faster pickup
LINK is nearly always faster than rideshare from the stadium
driving_parking: SODO District lots are available — pre-book strongly advised
Traffic on I-5 and I-90 backs up significantly after full-capacity Lumen Field events
Stadium lots closest to the venue fill within 90 minutes of kickoff
walking_biking: Pioneer Square, the waterfront, and Downtown are all walking distance from the stadium
Lime and JUMP e-bikes/scooters operate throughout the city
The waterfront path north toward the Pike Place Market is a beautiful post-match walk
match_day_tips: LINK is genuinely the best option — fast, frequent, and avoids all parking and traffic headaches
Lumen Field gets loud — the Sounders supporter section culture will make match atmospheres electric
Pioneer Square bars are a 5-minute walk from the stadium — arrive early for the pre-match scene
Cell service is strained inside the stadium — download mobile tickets in advance

fan_hubs.name: Seattle Fan Hub — Seattle Center
fan_hubs.description: Seattle Center — home to the Space Needle and the MoPOP museum — is expected to host a major fan hub with giant screens, Pacific Northwest food and craft beer, and live entertainment. One of the most photogenic outdoor event spaces in the country.
transport_tips: Seattle Center Monorail from Westlake Center Downtown — 2 minutes
LINK to Westlake, then Monorail to Seattle Center
Multiple bus routes serve the Seattle Center / Lower Queen Anne area

fan_hubs.name: Occidental Square Fan Block
fan_hubs.description: Pioneer Square's cobblestone plaza — steps from Lumen Field — is the natural pre-match gathering spot for Sounders fans and soccer supporters. Bars and restaurants surround the square. Expect it to fill hours before kickoff.
transport_tips: LINK to International District/Chinatown, walk through Pioneer Square

neighborhoods.name: Downtown / Pike Place
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Safe and active through the day. Use common sense at night near 3rd Ave transit stops.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: 10–15 min walk or one LINK stop to stadium
neighborhoods.description: Best central location with walking access to the stadium, Pike Place Market, and the Seattle waterfront. Strong hotel selection and easy LINK access.

neighborhoods.name: Pioneer Square
neighborhoods.best_for: Stadium proximity, arts, soccer bar scene
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Generally safe in the restaurant and bar zone. Some homelessness visible near certain blocks — normal Seattle context.
neighborhoods.description: Seattle's historic neighbourhood, directly adjacent to Lumen Field. cobblestone streets, galleries, and the densest concentration of match-day bars in the city. CitizenM hotel is excellent value.

neighborhoods.name: Capitol Hill
neighborhoods.best_for: Nightlife, restaurants, LGBTQ+ friendly, Seattle culture
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Safe and vibrant. Very active late-night scene.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: LINK to International District or walk via 1st Ave — about 20–25 min
neighborhoods.description: Seattle's most culturally vibrant neighbourhood. The best bar and restaurant density in the city. A bit farther from the stadium but the right home for fans who want the full Seattle night-life experience.

neighborhoods.name: South Lake Union
neighborhoods.best_for: Tech crowd, modern hotels, waterfront access
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Safe and modern. Lots of corporate hotels.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: LINK or bus to Pioneer Square — about 20 min
neighborhoods.description: Amazon's headquarters neighbourhood with newer hotels, good restaurants, and Lake Union access. More corporate feel but practical for business travelers who also want World Cup access.

hotels.name: Thompson Seattle
hotels.best_for: Boutique luxury, rooftop views, Pike Place access

booking_links.label: Browse all Seattle hotels on Booking.com →

bars.name: The George & Dragon
bars.notes: Seattle's most beloved English pub. Packed for every major international match. Arrive 45+ min early.

bars.name: Pike Brewing Co.
bars.notes: Classic Seattle brewpub at Pike Place. Multiple screens and a fun crowd on match days.

bars.name: The Innkeeper
bars.notes: Capitol Hill's dedicated soccer bar. Sounders fans know this place well.

bars.name: Central Saloon
bars.notes: Seattle's oldest bar — steps from Lumen Field. Expect it to fill fast on match days.

bars.name: Optimism Brewing Co.
bars.notes: Large Capitol Hill brewery with an outdoor beer garden. Popular for afternoon watch parties.

transport.summary: Seattle's LINK light rail is fast, reliable, and connects Sea-Tac Airport directly to downtown and the stadium. It's the clear best option for match days. Buy an ORCA card at the airport.
tips: ORCA card works on LINK light rail, Metro buses, and ferries — buy at Sea-Tac Station on arrival
LINK 1 Line: Sea-Tac to International District/Chinatown — 40 min, then 5-min walk to Lumen Field
Pioneer Square is walkable from the stadium — packed with pre-match bars and restaurants
Seattle weather in June–July is among the best in the tournament — walking is genuinely pleasant

fan_zones.name: Seattle Fan Hub — Seattle Center
fan_zones.description: Beneath the Space Needle — giant screens, Pacific Northwest food vendors, and live entertainment throughout the tournament.

fan_zones.name: Occidental Square Fan Block
fan_zones.description: Cobblestone plaza steps from Lumen Field. The natural pre-match gathering point for Sounders fans and all international supporters.

soccer_culture.community_notes: Seattle Sounders FC has set the standard for supporter culture in MLS since 2009. The ECS (Emerald City Supporters) and Gorilla FC are some of the most organised and passionate groups in American soccer. This stadium gets loud.
historic_venues: Memorial Stadium (LINK light rail expansion site)

tourist_hits.name: Pike Place Market
tourist_hits.notes: The classic Seattle experience — fish throwing, flower vendors, the original Starbucks. Go early morning.

tourist_hits.name: Space Needle
tourist_hits.notes: Iconic observation tower at Seattle Center. Book tickets in advance for the best views.

tourist_hits.name: Chihuly Garden and Glass
tourist_hits.notes: Extraordinary glass art museum at Seattle Center — one of the best art experiences in the Pacific Northwest.

tourist_hits.name: MoPOP Museum
tourist_hits.notes: Museum of Pop Culture — Jimi Hendrix, Nirvana, Star Wars, and Pacific Northwest music history.

local_favorites.name: Gas Works Park
local_favorites.notes: Former industrial gasification plant turned park on Lake Union — great city views and local crowd.

local_favorites.name: Fremont Sunday Market
local_favorites.notes: Arts, food, and vintage goods at Seattle's most eclectic neighbourhood market.

local_favorites.name: Kerry Park
local_favorites.notes: The definitive Seattle skyline viewpoint — best at sunset or on clear days.

local_favorites.name: Columbia City Farmers Market
local_favorites.notes: Genuine neighbourhood market in South Seattle — excellent Southeast Asian food stalls.

areas: Capitol Hill — best restaurant and bar density in the city
Pioneer Square — pre/post match bars right next to the stadium
Pike Place / Belltown — tourist-friendly with genuinely good food

recommendations.name: Canlis
recommendations.notes: Seattle's most celebrated fine-dining restaurant with stunning views. Book months ahead.

recommendations.name: Nue
recommendations.notes: Global street food done beautifully in Capitol Hill. Perfect for a pre-match dinner.

recommendations.name: Serious Biscuit
recommendations.notes: Tom Douglas's legendary breakfast spot — go for the biscuit sandwiches.

local_resources.emergency_info: Emergency: 911. Non-emergency Seattle Police: (206) 625-5011. Hospital: Harborview Medical Center, (206) 744-3000.

walk_bike.walkability_summary: Downtown Seattle, Pioneer Square, Capitol Hill, and Queen Anne are excellent for walking. The waterfront path and BellConnect trail are improving North-South walkability.
walk_bike.bikeability_summary: Lime and JUMP e-bikes operate throughout. The Burke-Gilman Trail is a classic cycling route.
walk_bike.bike_share_notes: Lime bikeshare and e-scooters operate throughout Seattle. Burke-Gilman Trail connects Fremont, U-District, and the waterfront.

pickup_soccer.name: Judkins Park
pickup_soccer.access_notes: Regular pickup soccer with diverse community crowd. Fields are open to public.

pickup_soccer.name: Georgetown Playfield
pickup_soccer.access_notes: South Seattle pickup scene with strong Latino football culture.

outdoors_day_trips.name: Mount Rainier National Park
outdoors_day_trips.difficulty: Easy to challenging depending on trail
outdoors_day_trips.notes: The iconic Pacific Northwest volcano. Multiple day-hike options from Paradise Visitor Center. Go on a clear day — Rainier is frequently cloud-covered.

outdoors_day_trips.name: Olympic National Park
outdoors_day_trips.notes: One of the most diverse national parks in the USA — temperate rainforest, alpine meadows, and Pacific Coast beaches all in one visit.

outdoors_day_trips.name: San Juan Islands
outdoors_day_trips.notes: Orca whale watching, cycling, and kayaking on beautiful Pacific Northwest islands. Washington State Ferry from Anacortes.

safety_tips: Seattle is very safe in tourist areas — Downtown, Pioneer Square, Capitol Hill, Queen Anne, and near the stadium
Use LINK light rail late at night rather than walking unfamiliar areas
Some visible homelessness near certain transit hubs — common in major Pacific Northwest cities, not a danger
Keep valuables in your hotel safe and be aware in crowded Pike Place Market areas
Seattle in June can still bring overcast mornings and light rain — always carry a layer
